Tarot on money and work: reading cards for business questions

2 October 2026

In business questions tarot works more precisely than in love: there are fewer projections here and more facts. The main thing is to choose what to ask about.

Which suit is responsible for what

  • Pentacles — money, income, savings, the material base.
  • Wands — career, ambition, initiative, launching projects.
  • Swords — contracts, negotiations, calculations, conflicts of interest.
  • Cups — the mood in the team, motivation, whether you like what you are doing.

If there are many Pentacles in a spread, the question really is about money and resources. Many Swords — about documents, terms and the precision of wording.

The cards that come up most often about work

  • Ace of Pentacles — a concrete opportunity, the window is open.
  • Three of Pentacles — teamwork, craft, recognition.
  • Eight of Pentacles — routine and learning: the skill that brings in money.
  • Six of Wands — recognition, promotion, a visible result.
  • Ten of Wands — overload: you are carrying more than you should.
  • Five of Pentacles — a hard stretch; the card often says that help is nearby, but nobody asks for it.
  • Five of Swords — an empty win: a victory that costs more than it was worth.

Three questions that work

  • “What do I need to change in my approach to money so that income appears?”
  • “Which of my strengths will help me get this position?”
  • “Which strategy will lead me to financial stability this year?”

All of them are about action, not about waiting.

What not to ask

  • “How much will I earn?” — the cards do not hand out numbers.
  • “When will I get a raise?” — exact dates never work here.
  • “Should I take out a loan?” — that is a financial decision, not a card one. Ask differently: “which risks am I not seeing in this deal?”

A three-card spread for work

  • 1 — Now: the real state of things.
  • 2 — What is in the way: the bottleneck you may not be noticing.
  • 3 — Where it leads: the direction at the current course.

If the third card is unpleasant, it is not a verdict but a description of where inaction will lead.

Lay out three cards on your work question. And write the conclusion in one sentence — decisions are easier that way.
